hints: Differentiate $x=\sec t$ to get $dx/dt$ in terms of $\sec t$ and $\tan t$.
Differentiate $y=\ln(\tan t)$ using the chain rule, keeping the factor $1/\tan t$.
Divide the two derivatives and rewrite everything in sines and cosines to cancel to the stated expression.
walkthrough:
Differentiate $x = \dfrac{1}{\cos t} = (\cos t)^{-1}$ with respect to $t$ using the chain rule:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = -(\cos t)^{-2} \cdot \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(\cos t) = -(\cos t)^{-2}(-\sin t) = \dfrac{\sin t}{\cos^2 t}$$

Differentiate $y = \ln(\tan t)$ with respect to $t$ using the chain rule:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} = \dfrac{1}{\tan t} \cdot \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(\tan t) = \dfrac{1}{\tan t} \cdot \sec^2 t$$

Express $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}$ in terms of sine and cosine:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} = \dfrac{\cos t}{\sin t} \cdot \dfrac{1}{\cos^2 t} = \dfrac{1}{\sin t \cos t}$$

Apply the parametric differentiation rule $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y/\mathrm{d}t}{\mathrm{d}x/\mathrm{d}t}$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{\sin t \cos t}}{\dfrac{\sin t}{\cos^2 t}} = \dfrac{1}{\sin t \cos t} \cdot \dfrac{\cos^2 t}{\sin t}$$

Cancel the common factor $\cos t$ to arrive at the required expression:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{\cos t}{\sin^2 t}$$

hints: First use $y=\ln(\tan t)=0$ to determine the parameter value in $0<t<\frac\pi2$.
Substitute this value of $t$ into $x=\sec t$ and into the gradient $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{\cos t}{\sin^2t}$.
Form the tangent through the resulting point using $y-y_0=m(x-x_0)$, then simplify.
walkthrough:
Find the parameter value $t$ at the point where $y = 0$:
$$\ln(\tan t) = 0 \implies \tan t = \mathrm{e}^0 = 1$$
Since $0 < t < \dfrac{1}{2}\pi$:
$$t = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$$

Calculate the gradient $m = \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ at $t = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ using the result from part (a):
$$m = \dfrac{\cos(\pi/4)}{\sin^2(\pi/4)} = \dfrac{1/\sqrt{2}}{(1/\sqrt{2})^2} = \dfrac{1/\sqrt{2}}{1/2} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}$$

Use the point-gradient equation of a line $y - y_0 = m(x - x_0)$ with $(x_0, y_0) = (\sqrt{2}, 0)$:
$$y - 0 = \sqrt{2}(x - \sqrt{2})$$

Expand to obtain the final equation of the tangent:
$$y = \sqrt{2}x - (\sqrt{2})(\sqrt{2})$$
$$y = \sqrt{2}x - 2$$
